novel_mechanics_found: Level 5 returns to one checked horizontal chain/guide pair, but splits the movable rack with a fixed blocker at x=29. The target guide order is 8 -> 9 -> 8; three 9 blocks begin left of the blocker and three 8 blocks begin right of it. The carrier must detour vertically around the blocker, stage blocks on different rows, and use endpoint passage plus selective retraction to assemble the target. A new boundary-jamming subtlety was verified: during horizontal retraction, a covered block whose push is blocked by the playfield boundary stays fixed while the chain retracts through it; during perpendicular row movement, an analogous blocked push cancels the whole row move.
narrative: The mandated resolver selected results/outer_loop_codex_sk48_probe_round8_20260712.json. A fresh env.reset() followed by all 106 labels reproduced frame_level 4 with GameState.NOT_FINISHED exactly. Live component dumps mapped L5 as a single horizontal checked pair with target 8,9,8, six movable rack blocks split into left-side 9,9,9 and right-side 8,8,8, and a fixed blocker at x=29. Five geometry-neutral live probes verified vertical carrying, the blocked forward extension at the divider, and retraction/extension behavior. A source-grounded settled-state transition model was refined against direct game-logic execution, including boundary and blocker collision behavior, then searched to a 33-action candidate. Every intermediate candidate state matched direct game-logic execution. Applied live after the five probes, the final ACTION4 changed frame_level 4 -> 5 at full-sequence label 144. A second fresh offline environment replayed the exact 144-label sequence and independently reproduced all transitions 0->1 at label 14, 1->2 at 44, 2->3 at 81, 3->4 at 106, and 4->5 at 144, ending GameState.NOT_FINISHED.
gotchas: L5 has one checked pair, not multiple simultaneous pairs: the bottom guide requires exactly the first three seen colors 8,9,8.
The fixed x=29 blocker prevents forward extension across it on the rack row and prevents a long cross-divider carrier from moving perpendicularly into that row; the chain must cross on another row.

A colored block moves with a horizontal push only when its entire same-direction push component has a legal destination. If the boundary or blocker jams that component, horizontal segments may pass through while the block stays fixed.
For a perpendicular carrier move, one jammed carried component cancels the entire row move rather than allowing the remaining components and chain head to move.

The five mapping probes are retained in the submitted action_sequence. They return the geometry to the exact initial L5 arrangement before the 33-action solve tail, but still consume energy and env.step calls.
FrameDataRaw.frame is an animation-frame stack on this game; authoritative progress is frame_level(frame) plus settled sprite/component coordinates, not a naive whole-stack array comparison.
The winning ACTION4 returns the next level in the same env.step call; label 144 is therefore both the final L5 gate action and the first returned frame at level 5.
